vibe: Ship a plugin that installs cleanly everywhere, or don't ship at all.
highlights: Ships-alone law: the published cadgen wheel must work in isolation, enforced by a boundary test that forbids references outside the package.
One launch command everywhere: uvx --no-config --managed-python --python 3.13 --from cadgen==<VERSION>, with every pin asserted equal to VERSION.
No symlinks in the published tree: installers disagree and Codex silently drops them, so check-builds.sh enforces a hard ban.
Every test runs in CI: a test no job runs is dead, and a collector finding nothing fails the run.
README holds the laws; the mechanism lives one link away — read the README, then follow the one link, not the tree.
assessment: This file treats distribution mechanics as first-class architecture: version pinning, daemon identity, symlink behavior across agent installers, and wheel isolation are all specified with enforcement tests rather than prose. The result is a repo where 'it works on my machine' is structurally impossible, because the shipping contract is checked on every push. The discipline around CI budgets, flaky tests, and self-contained fixtures shows a team that has been burned by silent failures and has converted each scar into a rule.
